lesson_title: Ceilings Make Queues, Floors Make Piles: Public Sector Intervention
hook_text: Cap the bread price and the bread DISAPPEARS. Here's why.
clip_script: Hard times. The state caps the bread price — cheap bread for everyone, right? Watch what actually happens. Buyers cheer and crowd in. But the bakers? At that price, baking barely pays — so they bake LESS. Many wanting, few baking: the shelves empty. And here's the cruel twist — the price can't rise to fix it. That's illegal now. So who gets the cheap bread? Whoever queued from 5 a.m. Whoever knows the baker. And in the alley behind the shop, someone sells hidden loaves at DOUBLE the old price — the black market, born straight from the gap between what's legal and what's scarce. Now flip it: hold the maize price UP to protect farmers, and they plant everything — while buyers take less. The silos overflow, and the state must buy the mountain. One picture holds it all: ceilings pushed low make QUEUES. Floors raised high make PILES. Intervene wisely — the market always answers back.
visual_style: A bakery scene: price tag slamming down, shelves draining, a dawn queue stretching; a shadowed alley handoff; then silos filling into a maize mountain; closing split-frame of queue-under-ceiling and pile-on-floor.
mood: Cautionary fable energy — vivid, fair, non-partisan.
pacing: Fast cause-and-effect chain, one beat per consequence, symmetrical flip, clean two-line landing.
